clips.text: On December first, 1984, NASA crashed a Boeing 720 airliner on purpose.
Nobody was on board. A pilot flew it by remote control from the ground.
The goal was to test a fuel additive meant to stop crash fires.
Before the real thing, the team flew fourteen test flights with crews aboard and practiced sixty-nine approaches to the crash site.
But in practice, the airplane had never flown lower than a hundred and fifty feet toward the crash site.
On the real flight, it arrived slightly off the centerline, and its left wing hit first.
The fuel ignited into a fireball that burned for more than an hour.
At full scale the modified fuel did not prevent a massive fuel-fed fire, and the FAA ended its attempts to require the additive.
